root_cause.text: nft_ct_timeout_obj_destroy() frees the timeout object synchronously with kfree() after nf_ct_untimeout() without waiting for an RCU grace period, allowing concurrent RCU-protected packet processing to access freed memory.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "frees the timeout object with kfree() immediately after nf_ct_untimeout(), without waiting for an RCU grace period" and the patch changes kfree() to kfree_rcu() by adding an rcu_head to struct nf_ct_timeout. The KASAN report shows a use-after-free in nf_conntrack_tcp_packet.

The KASAN report shows a use-after-free in nf_conntrack_tcp_packet.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add RCU head to nf_ct_timeout structure to enable proper RCU-based memory management and prevent synchronization issues.
intent_record.what: Added a struct rcu_head rcu field to the nf_ct_timeout structure.
intent_record.how: This change enables the nf_ct_timeout structure to be safely managed under RCU (Read-Copy-Update) semantics, allowing for deferred freeing or callback execution without causing use-after-free races.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential use-after-free by safely freeing the nft_ct timeout structure using kfree_rcu instead of immediate kfree.
intent_record.what: Replaced kfree(priv->timeout) with kfree_rcu(priv->timeout, rcu) in the nft_ct_timeout_obj_destroy function.
intent_record.how: The timeout structure is now freed via an RCU callback, ensuring it is not freed while still being accessed by RCU readers, thus preventing a potential use-after-free race condition.
